implementation: Public local and npm entry points dispatch standard Linux Lark uninstall to the existing v2 service lifecycle; npm uninstall performs no registry or pnpm-store work.

The transaction masks and stops every installer-managed unit bound to the canonical DSH_HOME, activates a copied clean profile offline, atomically swaps homes, and restores only units that were originally active.
Units, drop-ins, credentials, owner binding, Session, Goal, database, linger settings and external state are retained because their deletion has no separate crash-safe retirement transaction.

Foreign custom or legacy units are ignored only when unique absolute DSH_HOME and WorkingDirectory evidence both prove they are outside the target home; relative, ambiguous, nested or drifting ownership fails closed.
The v2 manifest binds the complete managed/foreign unit partition and foreign ownership digests, which are rechecked before mutation, rename, service acceptance, finalization, cleanup and recovery.

Same-home clean profiles from an earlier uninstall are accepted only when four exact installer files and the complete directory entry set match; every clean profile digest is manifest-bound and rechecked across restart, stability, finalization, cleanup and recovery.

Pre-swap failure restores the original home and active set; original-renamed recovery restores the original directory; post-swap failure preserves clean current and original backup homes and keeps services contained without automatic rollback.
A repeated uninstall of an already clean target with no managed top-level dependency is an idempotent no-op that does not touch systemd.
